calculation: Five measures (miles, back-to-backs, three-in-four stretches, time-zone crossings, back-to-backs against a rested opponent), each scaled 0 to 100 across the league, then averaged with equal weight. No opponent quality.
reproduced: Yes, from their own columns. Remaining differences look like rounding.

calculation: For every game still to play, add the opponent's current wins and losses. Teams are ranked by the resulting opponent win percentage.

measures: Opponent quality, games left and games played
calculation: Opponent win percentage is the plain average of opponents' win percentages. Opponent rating is the average of opponents' Elo ratings, with road games counting the opponent as stronger and home games as weaker. Power rank is the order of Elo ratings. Teams are ranked by average opponent rank.
reproduced: Win percentage and rank, to rounding. Elo, once a venue adjustment of roughly 60 points each way is fitted. Not the Elo ratings themselves.

measures: Opponent quality with venue and rest adjustments
calculation: Difficulty relative to an average schedule. Opponent strength blends a projected rating (built from players' ratings and minutes) with adjusted net rating. Adds home court, altitude and back-to-back adjustments.
reproduced: Partly. The opponent blend, about 60 percent projected rating and 40 percent adjusted net rating, explains nearly all the variation. The adjustments are too small to separate.

calculation: RPI is 25 percent own win percentage, 50 percent opponents' win percentage and 25 percent opponents' opponents' win percentage. Its strength of schedule works out to two parts opponents' win percentage and one part opponents' opponents', divided by three.
reproduced: The RPI to schedule-strength relationship, yes. The schedule-strength figure itself, not exactly, because the real RPI drops each opponent's game against the team.

calculation: Estimated flight distance between arenas plus a margin for weather. Flights are the trips between different cities, including the trip to the first game.
reproduced: Closely. Miles agree within a few hundred per team; flights run about one lower on our side.

measures: Wins lost to the schedule: opponents, rest, travel and the rest of each game's situation
calculation: Each game's win probability for a league-average team comes from point effects measured on ten seasons of results (home court, back-to-backs, distance, time zones, three games in four nights, altitude), with team strength fitted separately for every team and season. Opponents' strength is last season's fitted rating scaled by the share that carried over from year to year, measured against an even spread of opponents. Wins lost is the sum over the season of the drop from an even game. Noisy effects are pulled toward zero.
